heading: Section 1.01. - Incorporation.
path: ARTICLE I. - INCORPORATION; FORM OF GOVERNMENT; POWERS OF THE CITY; CORPORATE LIMITS
text:
The municipal corporation now existing as a metropolitan city and known as the "City
of Omaha" shall continue to be a body corporate and politic, and by that name shall
continue in perpetuity, with power to sue and be sued, to buy and sell real and personal
property, to contract, and to exercise all powers conferred by law on municipal corporations.

heading: Section 1.02. - Form of Government.
path: ARTICLE I. - INCORPORATION; FORM OF GOVERNMENT; POWERS OF THE CITY; CORPORATE LIMITS
text:
The municipal government established by this charter shall be known as the Mayor-Council
form of government, and its essential components shall be an elected chief executive
to be known as the Mayor and an elected legislative body to be known as the Council.

Code references—Council, § 2-21 et seq.; mayor, § 2-71 et seq.

heading: Section 1.03. - Powers of the City.
path: ARTICLE I. - INCORPORATION; FORM OF GOVERNMENT; POWERS OF THE CITY; CORPORATE LIMITS
text:
The city shall have all powers of local self-government and home rule and all other
powers that it is possible for it to have at the present and in the future under the
Constitution of the State of Nebraska. The city shall also have all powers that now
are, or hereafter may be, granted by the laws of the State of Nebraska. Except for
powers expressly denied it by this charter, the city shall also have all powers granted
to it or claimed by it in the Home Rule Charter of 1922, as amended, but the city
shall not be limited to these powers. All powers shall be exercised in the manner
prescribed in this charter, or if not prescribed herein, in such manner as shall be
provided by ordinance.
